name: Commodity roll yield carry
heading: The Structural Opportunity: Capturing Commodity Futures Roll Yield
caseLead: Commodity futures in backwardation can generate positive roll yield as their prices converge towards higher spot prices, even if the spot price is unchanged. Backwardation can persist when low inventories and limited spare capacity make immediate supply more valuable, particularly during sanctions, export restrictions and production disruptions.
caseRest: A fall in commodity prices can outweigh positive roll yield, especially when demand weakens or supply disruptions ease. Backwardated markets are usually those in which supply is already disrupted, so the end of a disruption or a drop in demand can reverse prices and remove the roll yield at the same time. A high carry return therefore gives little protection in the sharp falls that follow a supply shock, as in March 2020 and December 2022.
figNote: Each card shows the Brent crude oil settlement price, in US dollars per barrel, at the peak or trough of the episode. Brent is the main global benchmark for oil, so it shows how strongly energy markets moved while the strategy held its positions.

events.title: Oil oversupply pushes futures into contango
events.text: Rising US shale output and OPEC's refusal to cut production pushed Brent to about 28 dollars in January 2016, the lowest since 2003. The strategy gained because it was short in contango markets, where futures fall towards spot prices as contracts roll.

events.title: Attack on Saudi oil facilities lifts Brent
events.text: The 14 September 2019 attack on Saudi Arabia's Abqaiq facility cut about 5% of global supply and lifted Brent by 15% in one day to 69 dollars. Results were mixed because backwardation widened briefly, but prices fell back within two weeks as output returned.

events.title: OPEC talks fail as Covid cuts oil demand
events.text: After OPEC and Russia failed to agree production cuts in March 2020, Saudi Arabia announced higher output and Brent fell 24% in one day to 34 dollars. The strategy lost because backwardated energy contracts fell sharply and curves moved into contango.

events.title: Energy shortages lift oil and gas prices
events.text: Low inventories and a rebound in demand after lockdowns lifted Brent to about 86 dollars in October 2021, its highest in three years. The strategy gained because prices in backwardated markets moved up towards the higher spot price.

events.title: Russian invasion lifts Brent to a 14-year high
events.text: Russia's invasion of Ukraine and fears of lost energy exports lifted Brent to a settlement of 128 dollars on 8 March 2022, the highest since 2008. The strategy gained because prices rose across markets that were already in steep backwardation.

events.title: Recession fears reverse the oil price spike
events.text: Recession fears and weaker Chinese demand pulled Brent down to about 77 dollars in December 2022, below its level at the start of the year. The strategy lost because the fall in prices outweighed the roll yield earned.

instrument: Commodity futures across energy, metals and agriculture; rolled monthly
rules: Long the six most backwardated futures and short the six most contango futures, ranked by the annualised slope of the curve; sized by volatility; exposure reduced when the curve flattens
costs: Estimated bid-ask spreads, commissions and roll costs deducted at each monthly roll
constructionTitle: Strategy construction, from curve slope to drawdown control

legs.purpose: Earns the roll yield as prices converge upwards
Earns roll-down and diversifies the long leg
Limits losses in a demand-driven price fall
Provides collateral and earns the cash rate

entry: Curve slope of at least 5% a year in backwardation or contango
size: Set to a 9% annualised volatility target
exit: Position closed when the curve slope falls below 2%, or at the next monthly roll
stop: A position is closed if it loses 8% from its entry price
marketWatch: Inventory levels, the slope of futures curves in oil and metals and the pace of OPEC+ output decisions are key indicators. Rehyn tracks sanctions, export restrictions and shipping disruptions because they can tighten supply quickly and steepen backwardation. A sudden fall in demand or the end of a supply disruption matters because either can remove the roll yield within days.

favourable.heading: Tight inventories and supply disruption
favourable.text: Low inventories favour the strategy because buyers pay more for immediate delivery, which widens backwardation and raises the roll yield. After Russia's invasion of Ukraine in 2022, curves in oil and European gas moved into steep backwardation and the strategy earned a large roll return.

favourable.heading: Contango from oversupply
favourable.text: Oversupply favours the strategy because the short leg earns the roll-down as futures prices fall towards spot prices. Crude oil curves stayed in contango while Brent fell from about 60 dollars in mid-2015 to about 28 dollars in January 2016, so short positions gained.

favourable.heading: Steady demand growth
favourable.text: Steady economic growth favours the strategy because consumption keeps inventories low and curves in backwardation. In 2021, the recovery from Covid lockdowns lifted demand for energy and metals above supply, and Brent rose by about 50% over the year.

adverse.heading: Sudden fall in demand
adverse.text: A sudden fall in demand hurts the strategy because prices fall by more than the roll yield earned and curves flatten or move into contango. In March 2020, Brent fell by about 55% in a month as Covid-19 spread and a price war began.

adverse.heading: End of a supply disruption
adverse.text: The end of a disruption hurts the strategy because prices fall back to their earlier level and the curve flattens, so the roll yield disappears. After the Abqaiq attack in September 2019, Brent gave up most of its 15% one-day rise within two weeks as Saudi output was restored.

adverse.heading: Release of strategic stocks
adverse.text: Policy releases of stored supply hurt the strategy because they reduce tightness and flatten backwardation. In 2022, the US announced a record release of 180 million barrels from its Strategic Petroleum Reserve, and the Brent curve spread narrowed through the second half of the year.

infoHist: Historical results show the strategy's peak-to-trough drawdown during each event, measured from its value just before the event to its lowest point using the default backtest parameters above. Each event window runs from the last market high before the shock to the market low.
infoForward: Scenario results show the estimated profit or loss over the first month of each scenario. Rehyn's scenario engine projects moves in commodity prices, futures curve slopes and implied volatility, which are then applied to the strategy's current positions, including the protective options.

related.why: Follows price trends in energy, metals and agriculture. Bears reversals, losing when prices change direction.
Trades spreads between related contracts. Bears spread widening, losing when relationships between contracts break down.
related.cue: Targets spreads, not outright price direction

related.why: Trades supply disruptions using past episodes. Bears timing risk, losing when supply responds faster than expected.
